title: Staged cohort rehearsal with traffic reservoir and autorevert
author: Darren K. Morales
release_notes: Adds a rehearsal lane controller with reservoir-based shadowing and an automatic revert path when telemetry gates fail. No user-facing API changes. Backwards compatible with existing rollout policies.
description:
Motivation: we want a lightweight, low-risk way to rehearse model promotions using live traffic without impacting production SLOs. Existing shadow lanes either capture 100% of a chosen slice or mirror at fixed fractions; they lack a flow-control mechanism that prevents rehearsal storms and they require manual rollback procedures. This PR introduces a 'traffic reservoir' concept for rehearsal lanes: a bounded token pool that gates how many concurrent rehearse requests are admitted during a time window, plus an autorevert controller that automatically rewinds the rehearsal if safety gates are tripped.

Design summary: implement a RehearsalScheduler and ReservoirManager integrated into the rollout orchestrator. Key ideas: 1) Reservoir sizing heuristic derived from historical concurrency and SLO headroom; 2) Time-windowed token buckets per cohort to limit rehearse admission spikes; 3) Snapshot-based rehearsal mode that can playback a small sample deterministically for offline replay; 4) Telemetry tags (rehearsal_id, reservoir_token_id, cohort_tag) injected to tracing/metrics for direct attribution; 5) Autorevert runs a safe rewind (session-affinity-aware) and records a revert snapshot for postmortem.

What changed (high level): added services/orchestrator/rehearsal_scheduler.go, services/orchestrator/reservoir_manager.go, ops/playbooks/rehearsal-runbook.md, tests/integration/rehearsal_end_to_end_test.go, docs/rollouts/rehearsal-lanes.md and small hooks in services/orchestrator/traffic_router.go and telemetry/tags.go. The scheduler exposes a short-lived REST control endpoint for ops to query reservoir state.

Testing: unit tests for reservoir token lifecycle, integration test that runs a synthetic traffic burst and asserts no production latency regression, smoke runbook included for oncall. Telemetry includes a new gauge rehearsal.reservoir.available and histogram rehearsal.latency.replay.

Rollout plan: land behind feature flag rollout.rehearsal_v2; enable in staging for 48h with canary cohorts (1% of traffic, deterministic cohort id). After a clean staging run, enable in prod with gradual cohort increase 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 24h windows. Autorevert is enabled by default for rehearsals in prod.

Rollback and safety: autorevert is automatic when either (a) rehearsal error rate delta > 2x baseline AND > 0.5pp absolute, or (b) p99 latency regression exceeds 25% vs baseline for two consecutive windows. Revert is executed as a transactional swap with session affinity preservation where possible; if affinity cannot be preserved, revert will trigger a short-lived shadow replay of affected sessions to ensure correctness before commit.

Related: builds on ENG-2049 (cohort tagging infra) and ENG-2098 (telemetry gating primitives). See SUP-4821 for an incident that motivated automatic revert tooling.

Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] integration smoke [x] docs updated [x] runbook + playbook [x] alert rules for rehearsal.* metrics [x] feature flagged

Notes: this change is focused on rehearsal lanes (non-user-facing) and should not alter production routing unless the feature flag is turned on. The reservoir heuristic can be tuned remotely via ops API for emergency throttling.

review_conversation: Aisha Gupta: Can you clarify the reservoir sizing default? We should avoid a conservative default that blocks all rehearsals in smaller tenants.
Author: Default uses a 95th percentile concurrent baseline from 7d and adds a 10% headroom; ops can override via control endpoint. Updated comment in reservoir_manager.go.
Marco Chen: Race condition looked plausible in transactional revert path; please add a test that covers concurrent revert+promote.
Author: Added fix and unit test 'revert_race_test' and included a short-circuit to serialize revert/promote actions per cohort. See tests/unit folder.
Leah Ortega: Why are rehearsal tags at DEBUG level only? We need them at INFO for short-term debugging during rollout.
Author: Switched to INFO for first 24h post-enable and added sampling for long-term retention. See telemetry/tags.go.
